key_insight: Competing Ge-driven polar off-centering and Sn-favored octahedral tilting create a low-temperature phase boundary at x = 0.60–0.65 in CsGe₁₋ₓSnₓBr₃.
engineering_relevance: Ge/Sn mixing offers a composition-based route to tune polar order, octahedral rotations, and band gaps in lead-free halide perovskites.
method: Train a charge-aware machine-learned interatomic potential on hybrid-functional data.
Run large-scale molecular dynamics across the full Ge/Sn composition range.
Map composition–temperature phases and associated structural and band-gap changes.
evidence_signal: Simulations reproduce both end members’ known transition sequences and temperatures and reveal an intermediate I4/mcm phase absent from either parent compound.
watch_item: The predicted alloy phase boundary and intermediate phase require experimental validation before guiding device design.
paper_title: Competing Octahedral Tilting and $B$-Site Off-Centering Govern the Phase Diagram of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ Perovskite Alloys
